extracted.intended_audience: technology platforms, news aggregators, advertisers/brands, educational institutions, governments, researchers, and users seeking media-literacy/context about news sources
extracted.subtask_description: Describes NewsGuard's production of trust scores and Nutrition Label reviews for major news websites and a catalogue of top false narratives ('Misinformation Fingerprints'), including how those datasets are structured, distributed, and intended to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewsGuard Ratings (trust scores and Nutrition Label reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NewsGuard Ratings data consist of trust scores and detailed “Nutrition Label” reviews for the more than 6,500 news and information websites that account for 95% of online engagement with the news in the US, UK, Italy, France, and Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produced by a global team of experienced journalists; intended to give people more context for the news and information they see online; available for licensing to platforms, aggregators, brands, and institutions to inform decision-making and provide media literacy resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misinformation Fingerprints (catalogue of false narratives)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Misinformation Fingerprints are a catalogue of the top false narratives spreading online. The Fingerprint for each myth contains a description of the myth, a debunk of the claim, links to stories that have spread the myth, and associated keywords and hashtags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fingerprints are provided in machine-readable or human-readable format and can be used to seed AI/ML tools or train teams of content moderators; assembled by reviewing and monitoring the most-engaged news sources to identify narratives and the sources that spread them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trained journalists and experienced editors
rubrics_metrics.description: A team of trained journalists and experienced editors uses human intelligence — transparent, accountable, and apolitical reporting — to produce ratings and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes human review over algorithmic scoring: 'By using real journalists and a clearly disclosed process, NewsGuard is the opposite of an algorithm.' This implies a quality standard privileging human journalistic methods, editorial oversight, and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency, accountability, and apolitical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard describes its approach as transparent, accountable, and apolitical reporting used to give people more context for the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process is 'clearly disclosed' and intended to be non-partisan; this functions as an evaluative standard for how reviews/ratings are produced and communicated to users and clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage/scope criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the top news and information websites that collectively account for the vast majority of online engagement with news (over 6,500 sites covering 95% of engagement in several countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and monitoring prioritize the most-engaged sources to gain a 'birds-eye view' of narratives spreading across the news landscape; scope is explicitly international (US, UK, Italy, France, Germany).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and usability of data (machine-readable and human-readable outputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets (Ratings and Fingerprints) are provided in machine-readable or human-readable format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for practical downstream uses such as seeding AI/ML tools, training moderators, licensing to platforms, and embedding in media-literacy resources for end users and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended applications and clients
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard works with technology platforms, news aggregators, internet service providers, advertising companies, major brands, educational institutions, governments, and researchers to help them spot misinformation and give them more context for the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing is positioned as a way to inform organizational decision-making and to provide end-users with media-literacy resources; examples of trusted clients are given (e.g., WHO, Microsoft).
